title: CRLA/265/2007 of SMT. SASHI BALA AND OTHERS Vs STATE

paras.text:
Reserved Judgment
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
 Criminal Appeal No. 265 of 2007
Smt. Shashi Bala and two others .......... Appellants
 versus
State of Uttarakhand .......... Respondent

Mr. Raj Kumar, Amicus Curiae, present for the Appellants.
Mr. P.S.Soun, learned AGA, present for the State of Uttarakhand/ Respondent.
 JUDGMENT
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
. One Balbeer Singh wrote a complaint to the District
Magistrate, Uttarkashi on 08.05.2006 against the accused persons
alleging the commission of offences punishable under Sections
376, 313 and 120-B IPC by them. The same was registered as
case crime no. 1 of 2006 on 10.05.2006, at 3:00 p.m., in patwari
chowki Badgaon, District Uttarkashi. After the investigation, a
charge sheet against Shashibala and Mila Devi was filed in
relation to the offences punishable under Sections 313/120-B
IPC; charge sheet against Chatar Singh for the offence punishable
under Section 120-B IPC and charge sheet against Jagbeer Singh
for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 120-B and 313

2
IPC were filed before the Magistrate concerned. The case was
committed to the court of Sessions.
2. When the trial commenced and prosecution opened
it's case, charges against Smt. Shashibala, Smt. Mila Devi and
Chatar Singh were framed as regards offences punishable under
Section 313 IPC read with Section 120-B IPC. All the three
pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Charge against
Jagbeer Singh was framed with respect to offences punishable
under Sections 376 and 313 IPC to which he pleaded not guilty
and claimed trial.
3. As many as 08 prosecution witnesses, namely, PW 1
Dr. Sudha Singh, PW 2 Dr. Vinod Kumar, PW 3 Rajendra Singh,
PW 4 Dhanbeer Singh, PW 5 Km. Babli (victim), PW 6 Balbeer
Singh (complainant), PW 7 Pratap Singh and PW 8 Virendra
Singh were examined on behalf of prosecution. Incriminating
evidence was put to the accused persons in statement under
section 313 Cr.P.C., in reply to which, they said that the
prosecution witnesses were telling a lie and they have been
falsely implicatd in this case. No evidence was given in defence.
After hearing both the sides, learned court below convicted
accused-appellant Jagbeer Singh for the offence punishable under
Sections 376 and 313 IPC. Jagbeer Singh was sentenced to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years and a
fine of Rs. 10,000/- in connection with offence punishable under
Section 376 IPC; and three years' rigorous imprisonment and a
fine of Rs. 3000/- in relation to the offence punishable under
section 313 IPC. Accused-appellants Smt. Shashibala and Smt.
Mila Devi were convicted in respect of offences punishable under
Section 313 IPC read with Section 120-B IPC and were
sentenced to undergo three years' rigorous imprisonment and a

3
fine of Rs. 3000/- each. Aggrieved against the said conviction
and sentences, present criminal appeal was preferred.
4. Prosecution led the evidence through PW 5 Km.
Babita (victim). In her examination-in-chief, she said that about 1
& 1⁄2 years' ago (from the date of deposition), the accused Jagbeer
Singh met her in kuthar (cowshed). Jagbeer Singh put a
handkerchief on victim's nose, as a consequence of which she
became unconscious. Thereafter, accused committed rape with
her. When she regained some consciousness, PW 5 Babita
enquired from him (Jagbeer Singh) as to why he committed rape
with her? Then Jagbeer replied that he will marry her. After
deepawali festival, the accused brought a sweet box for her and
also gave her a Currency Note of Rs. 100/-. He said that he will
keep her as his wife. The accused was uncle (not the real one) of
the victim. Accused committed rape with her many a times, as
she worked as domestic help to him. She conceived a child. She
told the accused to talk to her parents. She disclosed to her
parents that she has conceived the child of Jagbeer Singh. When
victim's father inquired from Jagbeer, he declined. A panchayat
was convened but Jagbeer Singh did not come in panchayat. He
told the villagers that he wants to perform court marriage with
her (victim). On having agreed for the same, the accused took the
victim and victim's father towards Uttarkashi. Accused was
accompanied by his wife (Shashibala) and his sister (Mila Devi).
Instead of taking them to Uttarkashi, accused took them to
Rishikesh, where a room in a hotel was booked. Victim's father
was left in the room. Accused took the victim to a hospital, where
victim gave birth to a child. Smt. Mila Devi and Smt. Shashibala
told the victim that they were taking the child for bathing, but
they did not bring back the child. PW 5 did not know the name of
the hospital. She was kept in a hospital for two days. Accused

4
along with his wife and sister thereafter left the victim and her
father in a chauraha. Victim and her father went to their village
where he (father) informed the villagers about the incident, which
occurred to them. When the villagers went away then, Chatar
Singh took her inside the room and committed rape with her in
village Kamda. PW 5 proved her statement under Section 164
Cr.P.C. (Ext. Ka-3). Her father lodged a first information report
regarding the incident. She was medically examined in District
Hospital, Uttarkashi. In the cross-examination, PW 5 said that
accused Jagbeer Singh was the co-villager, who resided in
Badgaon. PW 5 too resided in the said village with her brother.
Her parents resided in another village (Chhan). She knew that
Jagbeer Singh was married and had children. kuthar is situated at
some distance of the house of PW 5. Initially PW 5 did not
disclose the incident which occurred to her to anybody. When the
accused gave sweet box and a cash of Rs. 100/- she accepted the
same. The accused also committed rape with her in kuthar as
well as in the fields after deepawali. She worked in the field of
accused, where also he committed rape with her. She knew about
the pregnancy when the same was in the advanced stage. She did
not know the name of the hotel where she was kept in Rishikesh.
She did not tell the doctor and staff of the hospital that she was
raped. When her father convened panchayat, the panches viz.,
Dhanveer, Rajju, Bichaini and Avender came. When she came
back to her house, there was profuse bleeding in her private parts
for 7-8 days. She said that she did not tell the investigating
officer that Chatar Singh also committed rape with her. Chatar
Singh was acquitted by the learned court below.
5. PW 6 Balbeer Singh (father of the victim) told that he
was an illiterate person. He said that his daughter was aged 16
years. He came to know about the pregnancy of his daughter only

5
when she came to see a mela (fare) in village Kamda. It may be
mentioned here that the victim was residing with her brother and
her parents were residing in a different village. When PW 6
enquired from her daughter, she said that the accused committed
rape with her last year. Jagbeer Singh was pradhan (head) of that
village. When PW 6 went to Jagbeer Singh, he said that he was
ready to perform court marriage with her. Accused told PW 6
that they will be going to Uttarkashi. Accused proceeded with
PW 6 and PW 5 to Uttarkashi. His wife and sister also
accompanied him but the accused instead of taking them to
Uttarkashi, took them to hospital in Rishikesh. Victim Babita was
taken to a hospital by Jagbeer Singh, Shashibala and Mila Devi.
They obtained his (PW 6's) signatures on a piece of paper. They
dropped the victim and her father on their way back to the
village. PW 5 and PW 6 too reached their village whereupon they
found that the victim was not in the village. She was then taken
to village Kamda and recovered from the house of Chatar Singh.
PW 6 proved his complaint (Ext. Ka-4), but in the cross-examination, PW 6 admitted that his daughter did not tell him
that Chatar Singh (acquitted) committed rape with her.
6. PW 1 Dr. Sudha Singh was posted in District
Hospital, Uttarkashi on 10.05.2006. She examined the victim,
aged 17 years, on 10.05.2006, at 2:30 p.m. She proved the
medical report (Ext. Ka-1) and opined that the patient must have
aborted. She delivered a foetus of a size more than 16 weeks. [in
statement under section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim said that her
foetus was aborted]. The medical officer also referred her to the
radiologist for ascertaining her age. The radiologist opined that
the victim was above 18 years of age. PW 2 Dr. Vinod Kumar
proved the report (Ext. Ka-2) and said that the patient was found
above 18 years of age on the basis of x-ray report.

6
7. PW 7 Pratap Singh Bisht, retired patwari was the
investigating officer, who conducted investigation at some
length, proved prosecution papers and said that, on 07.06.2006,
the investigation of the case was transferred to the regular police.
In the cross-examination, he said that nobody told him the name
of the hospital at Rishikesh, but he was informed that the victim
was aborted in Prasad Hospital, Rishikesh. He did not made
enquiry from Prasad Hospital in this regard. PW 7 was not aware
whether Narendra Singh (brother of victim) and Jagbeer Singh
were having inimical terms with each other or not? PW 8
Virendra Singh was the investigating officer, who conducted
investigation subsequently. In the cross-examination, PW 8 said
that he was not aware as to in which hospital, Balbeer Singh
(father) and Babita (daughter-victim) were kept (by the accused
persons).
8. It was clearly indicated by the victim that the accused
Jajbeer Singh committed rape with her and when she was in
advanced stage of pregnancy, the same was noticed by her father,
who was residing in a different village and only then the first
information report was lodged. The accused Jagbeer Singh made
false promises that he will marry with the victim. Believing on
his assurance that he will perform court marriage with the victim,
the victim and her father proceeded towards Uttarkashi, but the
accused Jagbeer Singh, who was accompanied by his wife and
sister, instead of taking them to Uttarkashi, took her to Rishikesh,
where her foetus was aborted in a hospital. When the rape was
committed, she was about 16 years of age and when her foetus
was aborted, she was 17-18 years of age. The extract of entry in
G.D. (Ext. Ka-6) demonstrated that the victim was taken forcibly
to Rishikesh, whereupon she was kept in a hotel along with her
father and thereafter, the victim was taken to Prasad Hospital for

7
abortion, wherein her foetus was aborted. The victim and her
father were left in lurch in Rishikesh. They reached in their
village on their own. Thereafter, the first information report was
lodged. Jagbeer Singh was village pradhan and the victim was
minor when the rape was committed. PW 1 Dr. Sudha Singh
indicated in the medical report that the patient must have aborted
or delivered foetus, which was of more than 16 weeks. Jagbeer
Singh, his wife Shashi Bala and sister Mila Devi accompanied
the victim to the hospital where the victim was aborted. The
abortion was without victim's consent. Shashi Bala and Mila
Devi accompanied the accused Jagbeer Singh and victim, right
from their village up to the hospital at Rishikesh. They
voluntarily caused miscarriage of the victim and such miscarriage
was not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving life of the
victim and thereby Shashi Bala and Mila Devi committed offence
punishable under Section 313 IPC. If the doctors of Prasad
Hospital at Rishikesh were not implicated as accused, the same
was the folly of the investigation. The offence punishable under
Section 376 IPC was proved against the accused-appellant
Jagbeer Singh beyond reasonable doubt. The offence punishable
under Section 313 IPC read with Section 120-B IPC was proved
against Shashi Bala and Mila Devi beyond shadow of doubt. The
court below has discussed the evidence in great detail and has
rightly come to the conclusion that the offences complained of
against the accused-appellants were proved to the hilt. There is
no scope of interference with the reasoned findings recorded by
the court below.
9. Consequently, the appeal is liable to be dismissed
and the same is accordingly dismissed. The judgment and order
dated 20.06.2007 passed by the learned court below, upholding
conviction of the appellants, is hereby affirmed. The conviction

8
and sentence recorded against the appellants by the court below
is upheld. Appellants Smt. Shashi Bala and Mila Devi are on
bail. Their bail is cancelled. They are directed to surrender
forthwith before the court concerned to serve out the sentence as
was awarded to them by the trial court and affirmed by this
Court. Accused / appellant Jagbeer Singh is in jail. Let a copy of
this Judgment along with the lower court record be sent back to
the trial court to make the convict / appellants serve out the
remaining part of the sentence awarded by learned trial court and
thus affirmed by this Court. A copy of this judgment be also sent
to Superintendent of jail concerned where the appellant Jagbeer
Singh is currently serving out the sentence.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.)
Dt. April 04, 2013
Kaushal
